_comment: IBM M&A history extracted from annual report filings. 'tier':'major' = deals >$500M or strategic significance. valueSource='filing' means the dollar figure was read directly from the report's Acquisitions & Divestitures note or cash flow statement; 'announced' means the figure comes from IBM's contemporaneous press release/8-K (also a primary IBM source, just not the annual report). All values in US$ millions.

deals.name: ROLM Corporation
deals.valueNote: 1984 annual report discloses $1,185M in convertible debentures issued for ROLM; total consideration ~$1.3B including cash component
deals.description: Acquired ROLM, a maker of PBX telephone equipment and military computers. IBM sold ROLM to Siemens in 1988 after the business underperformed.
deals.ibmLanguage: 1984 annual report: 'amounts expended for the acquisition of the net assets of ROLM Corporation'

deals.name: Lotus Development Corporation
deals.valueNote: 1995 cash flow statement: 'Acquisition of Lotus Development Corporation - net (2,880)'
deals.description: Acquired Lotus for its Notes collaboration platform, which became IBM's foundation for enterprise messaging and collaboration software.
deals.ibmLanguage: 1995 cash flow statement direct line item

deals.name: Tivoli Systems, Inc.
deals.valueNote: 1996 cash flow statement: 'Acquisition of Tivoli Systems, Inc. - net (716)'
deals.description: Acquired Tivoli to build IBM's systems management and IT operations software portfolio, now a core part of IBM Automation.
deals.ibmLanguage: 1996 cash flow statement direct line item

deals.name: Sequent Computer Systems
deals.valueNote: Acquisition announced and closed July 1999; press release cited ~$810M
deals.description: Acquired Sequent for its NUMA (non-uniform memory access) parallel server technology, strengthening IBM's high-end UNIX server line.
deals.ibmLanguage: 1999 CEO letter: 'Sequent Computer Systems strengthens the high end of our Web server line'

deals.name: Informix Database Business
deals.valueNote: 2001 CEO letter states '$1.1B for strategic acquisitions' total for the year, with Informix described as 'the bulk'; exact consideration not separately broken out in the note
deals.description: Acquired Informix's database software business from IBM's rival, significantly expanding DB2 market share. The Informix database products were rebranded under the DB2 family.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2001 annual report: 'The bulk of our acquisition investment was used to acquire the database assets of Informix Corp.'

deals.name: PricewaterhouseCoopers Consulting
deals.valueNote: Widely reported at $3.5B; closed October 2002. Filing references deal but annual note does not break out final consideration separately.
deals.description: Acquired PwC's consulting arm — 30,000 consultants — instantly creating one of the world's largest IT services businesses. Foundation of what is now IBM Consulting, generating $21B+ annually.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2003 CEO letter: 'PricewaterhouseCoopers Consulting, Rational software and 19 other companies in the past two years'

deals.name: Rational Software
deals.valueNote: Closed February 2003; widely reported at $2.1B
deals.description: Acquired Rational for its software development tools (UML, requirements management, testing). Now IBM Engineering Lifecycle Management (ELM), used in aerospace, defense, and automotive.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2003 CEO letter reference

deals.name: PC Division → Lenovo
deals.valueNote: 2007 Acquisitions note: 'total consideration agreed to on December 7, 2004 was $1,750 million which included $650 million in cash, $600 million in Lenovo equity and $500 million in assumed liabilities'
deals.description: Sold the ThinkPad PC business to China's Lenovo for $1.75B. IBM retained an 18.9% stake in Lenovo. Strategic exit from commoditizing PC hardware to refocus on higher-margin enterprise technology.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2007 Acquisitions & Divestitures note — prior-year disclosure

deals.name: DataMirror Corporation
deals.valueNote: 2007 Acquisitions note: 'total consideration the company agreed to on January 24, 2007 was $725 million which was paid in cash'
deals.description: Acquired DataMirror for its real-time data replication and integration technology, enhancing IBM's data management portfolio.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2007 Acquisitions & Divestitures note

deals.name: Cognos Inc.
deals.valueNote: 2008 Acquisitions note: 'acquired 100 percent of the outstanding common shares of Cognos for consideration of $5,021 million consisting of $4,998 million of cash and $24 million of equity instruments'
deals.description: Acquired the world's leading business intelligence and performance management software company. Became the foundation of IBM Cognos Analytics, now part of IBM's AI & Analytics portfolio.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2008 Acquisitions & Divestitures note (Note E)

deals.name: SPSS Inc.
deals.valueNote: Closed October 2009; widely reported at $1.2B. Filing confirms acquisition but exact consideration not captured in this extraction pass.
deals.description: Acquired SPSS, the leading statistical analysis software used in academia, government, and business research. Now IBM SPSS Statistics.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2009 CEO letter reference to SPSS acquisition

deals.name: SoftLayer Technologies
deals.valueNote: 2013 Acquisitions note: 'completed the acquisition of 100 percent of the privately held company, SoftLayer, a cloud computing infrastructure provider…for cash consideration of $1,977 million'
deals.description: Acquired SoftLayer, a cloud computing infrastructure provider, to establish IBM's global cloud delivery platform. Became the foundation of IBM Cloud.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2013 Acquisitions & Divestitures note (Note E)

deals.name: Merge Healthcare
deals.valueNote: Closed October 2015; widely reported at ~$1B
deals.description: Acquired Merge Healthcare for its medical imaging and clinical data management capabilities, strengthening IBM Watson Health.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2016 annual report reference: 'Merge Healthcare in 2015'

deals.name: Truven Health Analytics
deals.valueNote: 2016 Acquisitions note: 'completed the acquisition of 100 percent of Truven…for cash consideration of $2,612 million'
deals.description: Acquired Truven Health Analytics, a leading provider of healthcare data and analytics, for Watson Health. One of IBM's largest healthcare investments.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2016 Acquisitions & Divestitures note (Note F)

deals.name: Red Hat, Inc.
deals.valueNote: 2019 Acquisitions note: 'the Company completed its acquisition of Red Hat, Inc. for total consideration of $35.1 billion'
deals.description: IBM's largest acquisition ever — the largest software acquisition in history at the time. Red Hat's open-source hybrid cloud platform became IBM's defining strategic bet under Arvind Krishna, who led the deal as SVP of Cloud.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2019 Acquisitions & Divestitures note (Note E): 'total consideration of $35.1 billion'

deals.name: Kyndryl Spin-off
deals.valueNote: Kyndryl's market cap at separation on November 3, 2021 was approximately $19B. No cash consideration — IBM distributed Kyndryl shares to IBM shareholders in a tax-free spinoff.
deals.description: Spun off IBM's managed infrastructure services business as an independent public company (NYSE: KD). IBM's largest-ever divestiture by revenue — Kyndryl had ~$19B in annual revenue at separation. The spinoff allowed IBM to refocus entirely on hybrid cloud and AI.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2021 annual report: 'the separation of Kyndryl that occurred on November 3, 2021'

deals.name: Apptio (from Vista Equity Partners)
deals.valueNote: Closed August 2023; IBM press release cited ~$4.6B
deals.description: Acquired Apptio, the leading Technology Business Management (TBM) and FinOps software platform, to help enterprises optimize technology spending. IBM's largest acquisition since Red Hat.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2023 annual report: 'Apptio acquisition' referenced in cash flow discussion

deals.name: StreamSets & webMethods (from Software AG)
deals.valueNote: 2024 annual report: 'completed the acquisition of StreamSets and webMethods from Software AG…$2.3 billion'
deals.description: Acquired Software AG's data integration and API management platforms, strengthening IBM's hybrid integration portfolio for AI-ready data pipelines.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2024 annual report: 'acquisition of StreamSets and webMethods from Software AG…$2.3 billion'

deals.name: HashiCorp
deals.valueNote: 2025 Acquisitions note: 'Total consideration $7,433' (millions)
deals.description: Acquired HashiCorp, the leading multi-cloud infrastructure automation platform (Terraform, Vault, Consul). Extends IBM's hybrid cloud platform with best-in-class infrastructure-as-code capabilities.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2025 Acquisitions & Divestitures note: 'Total consideration $7,433 million'

deals.name: Confluent, Inc.
deals.valueNote: 2026 Q1 10-Q Note 5: 'Total consideration $11,590' (millions); $31.00/share cash, ~$11.3B equity value
deals.description: Acquired Confluent, the data-streaming platform built on Apache Kafka, to strengthen real-time data flow for generative and agentic AI across applications and APIs. Integrated into the Software segment.
deals.ibmLanguage: 2026 Q1 10-Q, Note 5 (Acquisitions & Divestitures): 'On March 17, 2026, the company completed the acquisition of all of the outstanding shares of Confluent ... Total consideration $11,590 million'

annualSummary._comment: Aggregate M&A spend per year from CEO letters/MD&A (where IBM discloses total acquisition spending). Captures the many smaller deals ($50-500M) not individually listed above.

2002.note: CEO letter: 'PwC Consulting, Rational software and 19 other companies'
